about.title: Helping Students Reach Top Chinese Universities
about.body: IFFI Consultant is a dedicated China study consultancy helping students from Pakistan and beyond achieve their dream of studying at top Chinese universities. With deep knowledge of the Chinese admission and scholarship system, our mission is to make the entire journey - admissions, scholarships, visa and pre-departure - simple, transparent and successful. We treat every student like family, offering honest advice and complete support at every step.
about.mission: To make studying in China accessible, simple and successful for every deserving student through honest, expert guidance at every step.
about.vision: To be the most trusted China study consultancy - known for transparency, results, and treating every student like family.
about.values: Honesty, dedication and student-first service. We never make false promises - your success and trust are everything to us.

faq.q: Is it expensive to study in China?
faq.a: No. China is one of the most affordable study destinations. Tuition is low compared to Western countries, and many students study on full or partial scholarships such as CSC, which can cover tuition, accommodation and a monthly stipend.

faq.q: Do I need to know Chinese to study in China?
faq.a: Not always. 60 of the 72 programmes in our current list are taught in English. Chinese-taught programmes ask for an HSK certificate (usually HSK 4 or 5) - and we help you prepare. Basic Chinese still makes daily life much easier.

faq.q: What scholarships can IFFI Consultant help me apply for?
faq.a: We assist with the Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC), Confucius Institute Scholarship, provincial scholarships and individual university scholarships, depending on your profile and programme.

faq.q: How long does the admission process take?
faq.a: It varies by university and intake, but typically the admission process takes 4-10 weeks. Most September-intake deadlines in our list fall in May and June, so applying early is very important.

faq.q: Which documents do I need to apply?
faq.a: Generally: passport (valid 2+ years), academic certificates and transcripts, a study plan or personal statement, recommendation letters, a medical examination form, a police character certificate and passport-size photos. We give you a personalised checklist.

faq.q: Is studying in China safe for international students?
faq.a: Yes. China is considered very safe, with modern campuses, good public transport and large, welcoming international student communities in most major cities.

faq.q: Do you help with the student visa?
faq.a: Yes. After your admission letter and JW202/JW201 form, we prepare your complete X1/X2 student visa application and guide you through the entire process.
Contact us on WhatsApp or fill in the contact form for a FREE counselling session. We will assess your profile and recommend the best universities and scholarships for you.

faq.q: How many marks do I need for a scholarship?
faq.a: There is no single cut-off. Universities look at your whole profile - grades, study plan, recommendation letters and timing. Many students with 70-75% marks still win scholarships when they apply to the right universities before the deadline. Try our free Eligibility Checker or send us your marks on WhatsApp.

faq.q: Can I practise in Pakistan after completing MBBS in China?
faq.a: To practise in Pakistan you must meet the Pakistan Medical & Dental Council (PM&DC) rules for foreign medical graduates, including its licensing requirements. Recognition depends on the specific university and your year of enrolment, so we check each university against the latest PM&DC guidance before you apply.
Not for English-taught programmes (60 of 72 in our list). Some universities ask international students to pass HSK 3 before graduating, and Chinese-taught programmes require HSK 4-5 at application.

faq.q: What are the total tuition and living costs?
faq.a: In our current list, Bachelor tuition before scholarships ranges from about 2,000 to 39,900 CNY per year (median about 14,000 CNY), MBBS from 26,000 to 40,000 CNY per year, and the Master and PhD offers are fully funded. Living costs are roughly 800-4,000 CNY a month depending on the city. Use our Cost Calculator for an estimate in your own currency.

faq.q: What are hostels and student life like?
faq.a: Most universities offer on-campus dormitories - shared rooms are the cheapest and many scholarships include free accommodation. Single rooms and off-campus options cost more. Campuses have canteens, sports facilities and large international student communities.

Chinese universities provide advanced laboratories, practical learning opportunities, and partnerships with leading technology companies.
Graduates gain valuable international experience and strong career prospects in industries around the world.

Institutions like Tsinghua University, Peking University, Zhejiang University, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Wuhan University, and Nanjing University consistently rank among the world's best.

blogSeeds.title: Top Scholarships for International Students in China
body: China offers several scholarships that help international students reduce the cost of education. Popular options include the Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC), provincial scholarships, university scholarships, and Confucius Institute scholarships. These scholarships may cover tuition fees, accommodation, monthly allowances, and medical insurance depending on the program. Students with strong academic records and complete application documents have a higher chance of securing scholarships. IFFI Consultant helps students identify suitable scholarship opportunities and prepare competitive applications.

body: A Chinese student visa is one of the most important requirements for studying in China. Students generally need an admission letter, JW202/JW201 form, passport, photographs, medical documents, and other supporting paperwork. The process includes receiving admission confirmation from the university, preparing the required documents, submitting the visa application, and attending any necessary verification procedures.
